2026-05-09T18:51:01.9629618Z 4. Do not push your changes. That will be done by the tool.

2026-05-09T18:51:01.9838805Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9839152Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9839452Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9849420Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9850241Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9850733Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9852249Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9853906Z >
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9854637Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9855375Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9855551Z ### How to Use
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9855765Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9856253Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9856917Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9857070Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9857430Z # Discover what tools a server provides
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9857927Z <server-name> --help
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9858159Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9858511Z # Get detailed help for a specific tool (type, required status, description)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9859171Z <server-name> <tool-name> --help
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9859463Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9859755Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9860791Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9862526Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9862715Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9862976Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9863445Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9863925Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9864646Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9865433Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9866980Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9867174Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9867488Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs):
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9868830Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9869342Z safeoutputs --help                                 # list all safe-output tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9870720Z safeoutputs add_comment --help                     # show types and required params
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9871569Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9872194Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9872368Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9872680Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9873199Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9873651Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9874466Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9875715Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9875916Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9876158Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9876547Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9878119Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9879611Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9879756Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9880384Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9881160Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9881934Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9882205Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9882671Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9883715Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9884453Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9884858Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9885037Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9885751Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9886593Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9886744Z ```bash
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9887348Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9888165Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9888810Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9889218Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9889587Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971004Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971600Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971791Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9971987Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9972825Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9974795Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9975695Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9976615Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9977502Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9977974Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9978123Z ### Notes
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9978325Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9978912Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9980512Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9981668Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9983615Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9984757Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9985830Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9986719Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9987335Z </mcp-clis>
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9987674Z <github-context>
2026-05-09T18:51:01.9988219Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-05-09T18:51:02.0000664Z # Weekly Real-World Testing
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0001070Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0002706Z Run DollarLint against a fresh, bounded set of public repositories, persist the structured result, and publish a Discussion report.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0003538Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0003699Z ## Workflow
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0003896Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0004114Z 1. Use the `dollarlint-repo` MCP server first.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0005248Z    - Call `real_world_history` to inspect `reports/real-world-results.json`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0006309Z    - Use it to avoid repositories that have already been tested unless the manual input explicitly asks for a rerun.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0007012Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0007174Z 2. Choose the corpus.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0008067Z    - If `CANDIDATE_REPOS` is a non-empty JSON array, parse it as the candidate pool. Each item should have `name`, `ecosystem`, and `cloneURL`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0009204Z    - Otherwise use this default pool, skipping anything already in history:
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0009705Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0010035Z ```json
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0010358Z [
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0011064Z   {"name":"gitea","ecosystem":"Go/TypeScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0013530Z   {"name":"vite","ecosystem":"TypeScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/vitejs/vite.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0014616Z   {"name":"prettier","ecosystem":"JavaScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/prettier/prettier.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0015674Z   {"name":"fastapi","ecosystem":"Python","cloneURL":"https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0016672Z   {"name":"ansible","ecosystem":"Python/YAML","cloneURL":"https://github.com/ansible/ansible.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0017633Z   {"name":"neovim","ecosystem":"C/Lua","cloneURL":"https://github.com/neovim/neovim.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0018606Z   {"name":"deno","ecosystem":"Rust/TypeScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/denoland/deno.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0019644Z   {"name":"grafana","ecosystem":"Go/TypeScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/grafana/grafana.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0021661Z   {"name":"pnpm","ecosystem":"TypeScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0022853Z   {"name":"huggingface-transformers","ecosystem":"Python","cloneURL":"https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0023998Z   {"name":"node","ecosystem":"C++/JavaScript","cloneURL":"https://github.com/nodejs/node.git"},
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0025000Z   {"name":"kibana","ecosystem":"TypeScript/Node","cloneURL":"https://github.com/elastic/kibana.git"}
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0025738Z ]
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0026043Z ```
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0026226Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0026687Z    - Select up to `MAX_REPOS` repositories. Prefer a small, diverse set over a huge one. Default to 5.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0028004Z    - If the default pool is exhausted, pick other well-known public repositories with distinct ecosystems and conventional config files.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0028814Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0028978Z 3. Prepare and run.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0029439Z    - Call `real_world_prepare_corpus` with `clone: true`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0031086Z    - If it reports duplicates, choose replacements unless this was an intentional manual rerun.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0032911Z    - Call `real_world_run_corpus` with the prepared `corpusDir`, `cacheDir`, and `outputArtifact`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0035097Z    - Nonzero validation exit code 1 is expected when real issues are found. Treat crashes, missing output JSON, hangs, and unexplained warnings as higher-severity product signals.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0036924Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0037099Z 4. Triage the output.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0037585Z    - Inspect the DollarLint JSON output artifact with `jq`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0038636Z    - Separate parsing, validation, schema, coverage, warnings, crashes, performance, and output-contract findings.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0040524Z    - Decide whether each finding is a real third-party issue, expected test fixture data, SchemaStore mismatch, parser compatibility gap, confusing output/reporting problem, or DollarLint bug.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0042883Z    - Summarize product recommendations before finishing the run. Each recommendation must include a strength label of `high`, `med`, or `low`, based on frequency, severity, reproducibility, and expected user impact.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0044098Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0046109Z 5. Persist repository memory.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0048999Z    - Call `real_world_record_result` with the title, corpus, cache directory, command, output artifact, repositories, findings, product recommendations with strength labels in `productDecisions`, and follow-up notes.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0051981Z    - Also append a factual narrative entry to `reports/REAL-WORLD-TESTS.md` using the existing report shape.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0054391Z    - If files changed, request a pull request through the configured `create-pull-request` safe output. Keep the PR title concise and mention the structured result file.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0056494Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0057540Z 6. Publish the report.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0062124Z    - Request one GitHub Discussion through the configured `create-discussion` safe output.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0063197Z    - Title: use the run date and a short result summary, for example `2026-05-09 - 5 repo corpus`.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0066794Z    - Body style:
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0067214Z      - Use `###` and `####` headings only.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0068228Z      - Keep the summary, result counts, notable findings, and product recommendations with `high`/`med`/`low` strength labels visible.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0069466Z      - Put verbose per-file details and raw warnings inside `<details>` blocks.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0070665Z      - Include the tested repository table, DollarLint commit, output artifact path, and workflow run URL.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0078307Z    - If Discussion creation is unavailable, the safe output may fall back to an issue; mention that the intended destination was a Discussion.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0080120Z 
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0081070Z Do not fabricate results. If cloning or validation fails before a meaningful corpus run, publish a short failure report with the blocker, partial artifacts, and the next concrete fix.
2026-05-09T18:51:02.0084532Z
